slot.brief: Given Kc and temperature for a gaseous equilibrium, calculate Kp (or ask for which reaction Kp = Kc).

stem: For $2\text{SO}_2(g)+\text{O}_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{SO}_3(g)$, $K_c=24.6\ \text{L mol}^{-1}$ at $300\ \text{K}$. Find $K_p$. Take $R=0.082\ \text{L atm mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.
working:
$\Delta n_g=2-(2+1)=-1$\n$K_p=K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}=\dfrac{24.6}{0.082\times300}=1.00\ \text{atm}^{-1}$

Independent check: Δn = 2 − 3 = −1, so Kₚ = K꜀(RT)⁻¹ = 24.6/(0.082 × 300) = 1.00 atm⁻¹.
solution:
For gaseous equilibria, $K_p=K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$, where $\Delta n_g=2-(2+1)=-1$.
$$K_p=\frac{24.6}{0.082\times300}=1.00\ \text{atm}^{-1}$$
